c.tagline: Gateway to the Amalfi Coast, with a medieval heart and a palm-lined seafront.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are metered with fixed supplements for the airport and Amalfi Coast runs; agree the fare in advance for longer coastal trips.

emergency.note: 112 is the single EU emergency number connecting to police, fire and ambulance; 118 reaches medical emergencies directly.

hood_landmark.Centro Storico: Via dei Mercanti Salerno old town

avoid.reason: Keep an eye on bags around the train station and port and on packed Amalfi Coast buses and ferries in summer.

hood_desc: Salerno's medieval heart, a warren of alleys along Via dei Mercanti leading to the Duomo (Cathedral of San Matteo) and up toward the Arechi Castle; best for visitors who want history, character and lively evening spots on foot.
The palm-lined seafront promenade with gardens, bars and gelaterie facing the Gulf of Salerno; central and scenic, great for strolls and dining with a sea view.
The busy area around Salerno Centrale train station and the Corso Vittorio Emanuele shopping street; convenient for onward trains and ferries and packed with mid-range hotels.
A residential seafront district west of the center with a small beach and local restaurants; quieter and handy for the port, suiting travelers wanting a calmer base.
A largely residential eastern neighborhood near the marina and Arechi stadium, with everyday shops and eateries; a low-key, local place to stay away from the tourist crowds.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink, though many locals prefer bottled for taste.

transit.hours: City buses run roughly 5:30 AM to about 10:30 PM; regional trains and the urban metro line run longer, and taxis cover the late-night gap.
transit.note: Salerno is served by Busitalia Campania (formerly CSTP) city and regional buses, a short urban metro/rail line, mainline Trenitalia trains at Salerno Centrale, and seasonal passenger ferries along the Amalfi Coast from the Molo Manfredi terminal.
transit.pay: Buy bus tickets in advance at tabaccherie, newsstands or machines and validate on board; single urban fares are cheap, and train and ferry tickets are bought at stations or the port.

bus: SITA Sud regional coaches to the Amalfi Coast
ferry: Seasonal ferries to Amalfi, Positano, Capri and Cetara (Molo Manfredi)

transit.m: Shuttle bus to Salerno Centrale station (~40 min)
Taxi to the city center (25-30 min)

tip.r: A cover charge (coperto) is usually added; tipping beyond that is not expected, though rounding up or leaving a few euros for good service is appreciated.
